ownerThemes.theme: An owner who chose the Brother on price says it has handled several king and queen quilts and singles out the knee lift and thread cutter; she does not do detailed free motion.
In Juki versus Brother threads, Juki owners describe their machines as heavier and quieter, and note the mechanical Juki needs frequent oiling; the Brother is positioned as the value pick.
Beginner quilting groups frequently ask PQ1600S or TL-2010Q, which shows the two are cross shopped directly.

crossShop.why: The head to head in this class; same speed and throat, the Juki is aluminum die cast and usually costs more
Dealer version of the Juki with a micro lifter and more feet, at roughly three times the Brother's price
For buyers who decide they want utility stitches and a 10 in throat instead of straight stitch speed
The question of whether to skip the domestic step and buy a frame longarm

editorial.verdict: The PQ1600S is the lowest cost route to 1,500 spm straight stitching with a knee lifter and a wide table. It competes on price with the Juki TL class and gives up the die cast body and dealer network in exchange.
editorial.whoFor: A piecer or table quilter who wants speed, a knee lifter and a big table for the least money, and does not need decorative stitches.
editorial.skipIf: You want one machine for garments and quilts (no zigzag or buttonhole), you want frame quilting with regulated stitches, or you value dealer service over online price.
editorial.keySpec: 8.7 x 5.7 in throat · 1,500 spm · straight stitch only · 7 feet and wide table included
strengths: 1,500 spm and 7 mm max stitch length at a domestic price
Pin feed option for slippery or thin fabrics, plus 4 level feed dog and pressure adjustment
Knee lifter, automatic needle threader, 7 feet and a 23.3 in wide table in the box
weaknesses: Needle system, lighting and motor specs are not published on pages found
Throat figures differ by source (8.7 vs 8.5 in)

facts.value: Manual: dial range reaches 5 to 7 mm; reverse stitch is always 5 mm when the dial is set between 5 and 7 mm. Maker page lists no stitch length. SMP spec copy lists Stitch Length: 5 mm.
facts.note: Our spec cites the maker page for 7 mm, but that page prints no stitch length. The 7 mm figure is only implied by the manual's '5-7 mm' dial wording; the dealer copy says 5 mm. Soft number: keep as disagreement.

facts.note: Maker calls it needle-to-arm space, so 8.7 in is the width claim. Sibling PQ1500SL maker page lists 5.7 x 8.6 in (needle to arm x front to back, per a Brother customer service answer in search snippet). Parts retailer figure of 8.5 in is not a maker figure.
